interest: This document is valuable to historians of pre-World War II international relations as evidence of Japan's cultural diplomacy and soft-power initiatives in Latin America on the eve of the Second World War. By sponsoring a visit of Argentine educators via the Japanese Association for the Fostering of Tourism, Japan sought to cultivate goodwill and bilateral ties with Argentina. The record also reflects the vigilance with which the U.S. State Department tracked foreign political and cultural influence across the Western Hemisphere.
keywords: Japanese Association for the Fostering of Tourism
overview: This file consists of a single U.S. Department of State cross-reference sheet dated August 11, 1939, referencing Despatch No. 75 sent by Ambassador Norman Armour from Argentina. The record indexes an official invitation extended by the Japanese Government to nine Argentine schoolteachers to visit Japan, with their expenses paid by the Japanese Association for the Fostering of Tourism. Originally filed under Decimal File 810.42711-SS Rates/8, this cross-reference note was classified into decimal file 894.42735, the category governing cultural relations, student/teacher exchanges, and Argentine attendance at educational institutions in Japan.

subfiles.about: Cross-reference note recording Despatch No. 75 concerning an invitation by the Japanese Government to nine Argentine schoolteachers.
subfiles.summary: This cross-reference sheet records Despatch No. 75 dated August 11, 1939, from U.S. Ambassador Norman Armour in Argentina to the Department of State. The despatch reported on an invitation extended by the Japanese Government to nine Argentine schoolteachers to visit Japan, financed by the Japanese Association for the Fostering of Tourism. The original paper was filed under 810.42711-SS Rates/8 and cross-referenced into decimal file 894.42735 regarding educational and cultural exchanges.
